title: Worse is better: the philosophy that shipped Unix and C
body: Richard Gabriel's 1991 essay argued that software succeeds by being simple and mostly right rather than complete and correct, because simple systems spread and get fixed in the wild. He half-criticised, half-admired the style he saw in Unix and C. The debate it started about correctness versus adoption never really ended.
source_hint: Gabriel, 'Lisp: Good News, Bad News, How to Win Big' (1991)
